$meta.name: Claude of Tanks design tokens
$meta.author: Kevin B. Liu
$meta.spec: brand-ui SPEC §4.2-4.14 (Direction B 'Premiere'); owner type ruling 2026-10-17 for the families
$meta.generator: tools/gen-tokens.mjs writes src/ui/tokens/tokens.css and src/ui/tokens/tokens.ts; tokens.selftest.mjs proves they match
$meta.rules: Colours are OKLCH sources emitted as hex. Components read semantic or component tokens, never primitives. Keys are CSS custom-property names without '--'.

modehue.$description: Each game mode's own hue (owner 2026-10-25: "use the unique colors for each modes icon again"). Seven are the battle menu's original hues; the other seven keep at least 8.4 ΔE from every mode hue, the accent, the teams and ink in every vision view, and every hue holds 4.5:1 on the plates (src/ui/tokens/modeColours.selftest.mjs).

settingshue.$description: Each Settings category's own hue (owner 2026-10-26: "color code settings so its easier"): its tab's glyph, its headings' rule and its rows' glyphs. Every hue keeps at least 9 ΔE (CIE76 and CIEDE2000) from the others, the teams and ink and 12 from the accent in every vision view, and holds 4.5:1 on the plates (src/ui/tokens/settingsColours.selftest.mjs).

tungsten.$description: The one brand amber; tungsten-500 replaces the ~58 near-duplicate ambers in use

family.$description: Owner ruling 2026-10-17: Chakra Petch (display 500/600/700), IBM Plex Sans (body 400/500/600), IBM Plex Mono (data 400/500), all SIL OFL, self-hosted by the type package. CJK uses system faces after the Latin face.

font-display.value: 'Chakra Petch','Cot Symbols','Cot Display Fallback','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC',sans-serif
font-display.$use: Display moments: Chakra Petch, then the marks face and the metric-matched local fallback (src/ui/typeFaces.ts TYPE_STACK.display, which tokens.selftest.mjs holds equal), then the CJK system faces

font-body.value: 'IBM Plex Sans','Cot Accents','Cot Symbols','Cot Body Fallback','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC',sans-serif
font-body.$use: Reading text: IBM Plex Sans, the accents and marks faces, the metric-matched fallback, then the CJK system faces (equal to src/ui/typeFaces.ts TYPE_STACK.body)

font-mono.$use: Live readouts (tabular figures through .num only): IBM Plex Mono, then its metric-matched fallback (equal to src/ui/typeFaces.ts TYPE_STACK.mono)

family.font-cjk: 'IBM Plex Sans','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC','Source Han Sans SC',sans-serif

scale.$description: Runtime scale switches. --cot-ui-scale (0.78-1.08) is written by responsiveLayout.ts today. Nothing writes --cot-hud-fit (clamp(shortSide/1080,.85,2)) or the user factors (Text size 0.8-2.0, HUD size 0.75-1.5) yet: the accessibility core (BUI-F9) and the HUD restyle (BUI-H1) add those writers, so until then --cot-hud-scale is 1 and --cot-type-scale follows --cot-ui-scale alone.

font-size.$description: CSS px at 100 %. Nothing a player must read is below 11 px.

space.$description: 4 px base; retires the off-grid 5/7/9/13 px values

ease-exit.$use: At about 70 % of the enter duration

ease-move.$use: In-place travel (the shipped --cot-ease-move curve, kept so its consumers keep their feel)

font.$use: The reading face (SPEC 4.14 --font, owner ruling: IBM Plex Sans). Shell controls read --font-ui, display moments --font-display, live readouts --font-mono.

font-ui.value: 'Cot UI','Cot Accents','Cot Symbols','Cot Fallback','PingFang SC','Hiragino Sans GB','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC',sans-serif
font-ui.$use: The shell's weight-voiced family every surface renders ('Cot UI': Plex Sans 400/500, Chakra Petch 600/700), equal to FONT_STACK in src/ui/fonts.ts and to src/ui/typeFaces.ts TYPE_STACK.ui (canvas text cannot read var(), so fonts.ts repeats the literal)

font-data.$use: The direction's data voice (streams/brand-ui/phase2/bui01 --font-data): readouts, rules and codes; an alias of --font-mono

surface-nav.$use: The public bar's ground under its translucent veil (publicNav.css, home.css)

surface-plate.$use: Shell plates over stills and the live garage

atmosphere.$description: Scene light a page paints with, never a status or a team: no colour-vision preset remaps it

ink-4.$never: Any text a player must read

line.$description: SPEC 4.3 gives line-1/2/3 (paper-50 at 7 / 13 / 24 %, pinned to the 4.14 sheet) to hairlines, control borders and strong rules, and SPEC 4.4 requires every control border a player must perceive to reach 3:1. line-2 measures 1.38-1.44:1, so the three lines stay decoration and the control border is its own token, --line-control, measured at 3:1 or more on every surface and plate

line-1.$never: The only boundary of a control (--line-control)

line-2.$use: Card and menu rings (e2, e3) and dividers (decoration)
line-2.$never: The only boundary of a control (--line-control)

line-3.$never: The only boundary of a control (--line-control)

line-control.$use: Control borders: secondary buttons, chips, inputs, toggles, checkboxes (SPEC 4.4: >= 3:1 on page, raised, menu, hover and both plates over bright imagery)

accent.$use: Primary action fill, selection edge, wordmark rule
accent.$never: Warnings, objectives, module identity, rewards, decoration

focus-ink.$description: Focus is neutral (lead, 2026-10-26, after the Garage r25 critic read a focused card's tungsten ring as a second selected look): the kit's one selected state is the accent's wash and edge, so a focus ring or a focus outline never wears the accent.

focus-ink.$use: A :focus-visible outline's colour, where the box-shadow ring cannot sit

mode.$description: A mode's glyph colour wherever the mode is drawn (UI-GAUNTLET bar line 6): mark the element data-mode-tone=<mode id> and paint the glyph var(--mode-ink) (components.css). Mode identity is the glyph's shape; the hue reinforces it. Selection, the primary action and text stay the kit's.

settings.$description: A Settings category's colour (UI-GAUNTLET bar line 6's exception, as the modes'): the panel marks its tabs and its body data-settings-tone=<category>, and the tab glyph, the headings' rule, the selected tab's mark and the rows' glyphs paint var(--settings-ink) (settings.ts). Never text: the labels, the values and the selection stay the kit's.

settings-controls.$use: The controls category's glyphs and rules

settings-gameplay.$use: The gameplay category's glyphs and rules

settings-sound.$use: The sound category's glyphs and rules

settings-graphics.$use: The graphics category's glyphs and rules

settings-accessibility.$use: The accessibility category's glyphs and rules

settings-language.$use: The language category's glyphs and rules

team-own.$use: Allies everywhere, drawn as a chevron

team-enemy.$use: Enemies everywhere, drawn as a diamond
team-enemy.$never: Danger state in the same element

team-squad.$use: Squad, the player's own marker accents, drawn as a dot

warn.$use: Damaged modules, caution; always with the 45° hatch

text-tone.$description: Coloured text: team names, state words, accent counts and text buttons. Each reads its colour role, and the high-contrast preset turns every one to ink-1 (SPEC 4.6: all text ink-1 or ink-2, 7:1), leaving the colour to the glyph beside the word. Text over imagery sits on a plate; vermilion text needs the .92 HUD plate

text-enemy.$never: Text on --surface-plate over bright imagery (4.23:1 over white): the .92 HUD plate

text-danger.$use: Destroyed or critical words, beside the cross
text-danger.$never: Text on --surface-plate over bright imagery (4.23:1 over white): the .92 HUD plate

text-accent.$use: Accent-coloured counts, text buttons and links (the one brand amber)

outcome.$description: Okabe-Ito based; analysis contexts only (Gallery protection, hit cam, shot report, kill cam, docs), never the HUD reticle. Ricochet is striped; spaced/no-damage is a dotted outline only.

protection.$description: Clipped cividis, thin = bright, absolute mm: <40, 80, 180, 350, 500, 650, 650+. Luminance falls monotonically so the ramp reads in greyscale.

system.$description: Anatomy identity, always with glyph + label; state is pattern + colour

role.$description: Crew roles: the letter glyph is mandatory (deutan ΔE between roles falls to ~9.5)

elevation.$description: Plates, not glass. backdrop-filter is never used over a live WebGL canvas.

e1-flush.$use: e1 with its edge drawn inside the box, for a plate that shares a column edge with the content around it (Settings sections)

e2-flush.$use: e2 with its edge drawn inside the box, for a panel whose edge meets a neighbour's (the Deploy plate beside the mode grid)

e3-span.$use: e3 with the menu's plate under its ring, for a menu spanning a panel: its ring lies on the panel's rule and shows nothing of what runs under that rule

inset.$description: Shell edges: max(24 px, 3 % of the short side) + the safe area; the HUD adds the crosshair safe zone

print.$description: Tokens only the Field Manual printed reads (src/docs/docsPrint.css): the paper's inks, lines, accent and tones, and the print-safe type stacks. Semantic (they read the ramps); their own sheet, which only the print sheet imports, and their own module, so neither the game's tokens.css nor its tokens.ts carries them (docsPrint.selftest)

print-ink-1.$use: Text on paper (the Field Manual printed): the screen's ink-1

print-ink-4.$use: Faint text on paper (still 4.5:1 on white)

print-accent-lo.$use: The accent's dark step on paper

print-text-ok.$use: OK text on paper: its hue darkened toward the ink

print-font-ui.value: 'Cot UI','Cot Accents','Cot Symbols','Cot Fallback','Hiragino Sans GB','PingFang SC','Microsoft YaHei','Noto Sans CJK SC',sans-serif
print-font-ui.$use: The UI stack printed: Hiragino Sans GB before PingFang SC, whose glyphs Chrome's PDF drops

print-font-mono.value: 'IBM Plex Mono','Cot Mono Fallback','Hiragino Sans GB',ui-monospace,monospace
print-font-mono.$use: The mono stack printed: Chinese falls back to Hiragino Sans GB

shape.$description: 2 px for plates, controls and chips (the direction draws them all at 2 px), 4 px for cards and sheets; circles only for joysticks, blips and dials

button.$description: SPEC 6.1-6.2: one primary per view; heights 36 / 48 / 56 / 64 px; pressed = 1 px drop + accent-lo (primary) or the strong rule (others); disabled = ink-4, never hatch

target-min.$use: Minimum hit area of any control (icon buttons draw 36 px on dense desktop rails inside it)

btn-secondary-fill.$use: Secondary: 6 % paper fill with the control border

btn-press-edge.$use: Pressed secondary and danger buttons: the edge steps up from the control border to the label ink

btn-danger-edge.$use: Danger: vermilion outline + glyph; destructive actions take a confirm step

btn-primary-bevel.$use: The primary button's machined edge: a top highlight and a bottom shade inside the fill (SPEC 4.9)

chip.$description: Chips, filter chips and tags as the direction draws them (bui01 components.css .chip/.tag): 2 px, a hairline ring, a faint paper fill; selected = accent wash + accent ring

chip-edge.$use: A chip's control edge at the 3:1 floor (SPEC 4.4); the kit's chips draw the direction's hairline with --ring-2

selected-edge.$use: Selected state: accent edge on the leading side or a full outline

kit.$description: The Premiere direction's shared kit (streams/brand-ui/phase2/bui01/src/components.css and its pages): rings, quiet fills, media fades and the primary glow, so every surface ports the direction's CSS onto tokens

ring-1.$use: A hairline ring inside a quiet tile or row

ring-3.$use: Secondary buttons and glyph plates over pictures

ring-accent.$use: A selected chip, tile or card

btn-secondary-ring.$use: A secondary button's edge drawn inside it (Deploy's Watch)

btn-secondary-ring-hover.$use: That edge under a hovering pointer

ring-ok.$use: An OK tag or ready equipment

ring-hot.$use: A technical drawing's hot callout: the number badge on the plate and its row's number while that part is pointed at

z-lift.$use: Type and controls above a picture card's fade

z-under.$use: A picture behind a plate's content, over the plate's own fill (Deploy's mode picture)

fill-quiet.$use: Tiles, rule cells, segmented tracks, the tank card

fill-scale.$use: The 20-cell scale's empty cells and progress tracks

btn-primary-shadow.$use: The primary button: the plain e2 drop, no bevel and no coloured glow (the lead's ruling; elevation is e1-e4, the gauntlet bar line 6)

kbd-on-accent-ink.$use: A key cap on a tungsten fill

seg-on-shadow.$use: Legacy name of the selected edge: the kit has one selected state, the accent's wash and edge, on a segmented option as on a chip, a picked card and a toggle (Main, 2026-10-26)

glyph-plate.$use: A glyph plate over a picture (mode cards)

side-plate.$use: A docked side plate over the page

media-fade.$use: Under a title on the foot of a picture card

media-fade-soft.$use: Under a caption on a picture (battlefield art, takes)

media-fade-full.$use: Under a block of copy on a picture (campaign card)

type-effect.$description: Owner UI rule 5 (2026-10-17): display moments use the accent colour or the landing's hollow outline type, deliberately and at display sizes only (44 px and up). The landing's Latin headline is truly hollow (src/presentation/home.css .v5-hero-copy h1 span: color:transparent; -webkit-text-stroke:1.5px; text-shadow 0 8px 28px, pinned by tokens.selftest.mjs). The type package's .t-hollow reads --hollow-stroke and --hollow-ink. Never on CJK (SPEC 4.7): zh display type stays solid.

hollow-stroke.$use: -webkit-text-stroke width of hollow display type (the landing headline's 1.5 px)

hollow-fill.$use: Hollow type has no fill (the landing's color:transparent); never paint-order tricks, which cover the stroke's inner half

hollow-shadow.$use: text-shadow of hollow type: the landing headline's, which keeps the 1.5 px outline readable over bright media

stage-halo.$use: text-shadow of type set straight on the 3D stage (the garage lower third), readable over the turntable's bright rim

stage-scrim.$use: A soft local shade under type on the 3D stage; it darkens only the floor behind the words

hud-font.$use: HUD copy (battleHudLayout.css and hud.ts read var(--hud-font)): the shell family, as each document's type head declares it (typeFaces.ts typeTokenCss)

hud-type.$description: HUD floors at 1080p: 13 px copy, 14 px body, 20 px numerals

focus-bracket.$description: Registration brackets on cards, 3D picks, roster tiles and gamepad focus: focus is a shape, not only a colour

media.$description: The shared media player (src/presentation/mediaPlayer.css): its control sits above the frame it plays in

warn-hatch.$use: 45° damaged hatch spacing (deutan/protan presets double the density)

team-squad-ring.$use: Squad ring width (the tritan preset draws the ring)

surface-deploy.$description: Tokens only the Deploy screen reads: its direction page's values (bui01/src/pages/04-deploy.html, 91-phone-deploy.html)

surface-garage.$description: Tokens only the Garage reads: its direction page's values (bui01/src/pages/05-garage.html)

surface-home.$description: Tokens only the public landing reads: its direction page's values (bui01/src/pages/01-03, 90)

home-hero-grade.$use: The hero reel's grade: gradients only, never blur over imagery; the nav bar's band above, the counts at the foot ending on the page's own ink, so the hero meets the page without a seam (the mark and name are the nav bar's since 2026-10-25; the words have their own scrim)

home-hero-scrim.$use: The plate under the hero's words (the headline, its line, the shot's caption), feathered at its edges: their contrast holds over the brightest reel frame, snow included (owner 2026-10-25)

home-phone-grade.$use: The phone hero's grade (90 .grade), fading into the page; its lower half carries the words' scrim (home-hero-scrim's ink) down through the counts, so no plate edge crosses the picture

home-headline-shadow.$use: The hero headline's solid lines over the sky (01 h1 .line)

home-vs-ring.$use: The VS box of a named duel (01 .versus, 02 .t-big .vs)

home-pick-ring.$use: The tile or map card in focus (03 .tile.playing, .map.lead)

home-inset-ring.$use: A minimap inset over map art (03 .map .mm)

home-idx-ink.$use: A tile's index numeral over its picture (02 .idx)

home-closing-grade.$use: The closing band's grade (the landing's last call and the 404): the words' side darkened, fading into the page

home-reddit.$use: Reddit's own orange: its glyph, avatars and community names in the landing's social proof

home-card-z.$use: A social card's accent rule above its picture and copy

surface-docs.$description: Tokens only the Field Manual reads: its direction page's values (bui01/src/pages/08-docs.html)

docs-banner-fade.$use: The chapter banner's fade under its title (08 .banner::after), its side easing out (a straight ramp left a seam over a flat sky on a phone)

docs-side-on.$use: The current chapter on the shelf, a place in the navigation and not a choice: a slate plate, not an accent edge (08 .side a.on)

docs-toc-on.$use: The reader's place in On this page: its ink and weight carry it, no edge bar (08 .toc .lst a.on)

docs-hc-flag-mask.$use: The tank hero cards' flag feather (src/docs/chapters/fleet.ts): heroFlagMaskCss() for the left-facing policy; src/docs/topics.selftest.mjs holds them equal

docs-banner-z.$use: The banner's title and caption above its fade

surface-pad.$description: Tokens only the phone controller reads (site/pad.html): the control panel's metal, rubber, glass and lamps (owner 2026-10-30: "make it look more realistic")

pad-panel.$use: The control panel's face: gunmetal lit from above, falling darker toward the hands

pad-brush.$use: The panel's brushed grain, laid over pad-panel

pad-well.$use: A recess cut into the panel: the throttle's gate, the switch plates, the counter windows

pad-well-shadow.$use: A recess's depth: shade under its upper lip, light on its lower edge

pad-key-shadow.$use: A push-button standing proud of the panel: its lit top edge, its skirt and its cast shadow

pad-key-down.$use: A push-button held down: the skirt gone and the cap shaded, beside its 2 px travel

pad-lamp-on.$use: A lit amber lamp lens: the shell loaded, the sight engaged

pad-lamp-glow.$use: The light a lit amber lamp throws

pad-rubber.$use: A rubber grip's ribs: the throttle's handle, the brake

pad-bezel.$use: A turned-metal bezel: the instruments' rims and the fire button's collar

pad-bezel-shadow.$use: A bezel standing on the panel

pad-glass.$use: An instrument's face under glass, its glare at the upper left

pad-glass-shadow.$use: The bezel's shadow on the glass

pad-sight.$use: The gunner's sight: a dark optic inside its eyepiece's vignette

pad-fire.$use: The fire button lit: the gun is loaded

pad-fire-dim.$use: The fire button dark while the gun loads

pad-fire-glow.$use: The lit fire button's dome and the light it throws

pad-guard.$use: A switch guard's red cover over a consumable's switch

pad-guard-shadow.$use: A switch guard's moulded edge and its shadow

pad-bat.$use: A toggle switch's chrome bat, under its guard

pad-engrave.$use: Lettering engraved in a cap or the panel

pad-led-ok.$use: The link lamp lit green: the direct link

pad-led-warn.$use: The link lamp lit amber: linking, the relay or the desktop away

pad-led-glow.$use: A lit link lamp's light, in its state's colour

pad-counter.$use: A mechanical counter's drum seen through its window: the rounds left, the speed

surface-gallery.$description: Tokens only the Tank Gallery reads: its direction page's values (bui01/src/pages/07-gallery.html)

gallery-stage.$use: The stage's lit floor (.stage): the menu surface's step under the model, the page at its edge

gallery-row-on.$use: The selected fleet row's whole ring, never one coloured edge (.fam .it.on)

gallery-take-fade.value: linear-gradient(0deg,{surface-page} 0,oklch(from {surface-page} l c h / .5) 30%,oklch(from {surface-page} l c h / 0) 55%)
gallery-take-fade.$use: The take's foot, under the vehicle's name (.take::after)

gallery-dot-ring.$use: The ring that seats a callout's anchor dot on the model

gallery-reveal-after.$use: When the panes the script fills show anyway, for a script that never runs (.gallery-ready): a timeout, not a motion, so the reduced-motion preset keeps it, and past the slow-phone profile's first render (247: at 4.2 s the empty dossier showed, then reflowed)

surface-deploy.$description: Tokens only the Deploy screen reads (deploy.css imports the sheet)

plate-art-grade.$use: Over the mode's picture behind Deploy's plate: its words at 4.5:1 and its glyphs at 3:1 over every mode's picture, the picture clearest at the plate's head

plate-art-grade-open.$use: The plate's grade while the further options are open: their captions and values sit on the picture itself, at 4.5:1 over every mode's picture

plate-chip-fill.$use: A chip over the mode's picture on Deploy's plate: its fill on the opaque plate (a background value)

plate-chip-fill-on.$use: A lit chip over the mode's picture: its wash on a plate, so its colour holds from mode to mode

surface-diagram.$description: Tokens only the technical diagrams read (253): their tones, the inspection overlay's palette (src/gallery/overlays.ts paints the resolved values from the group's module, surface-diagram.ts, so the boot's tokens.ts carries none). A callout, pin, leader or legend swatch is marked data-tone=<tone> and technicalDiagramLabels.css maps it to --tdl-tone; that sheet imports this one

surface-badge.$description: Tokens only the item badges read (equipIcons.ts, 261): each badge category's frame colour, the equipment picker's five and the consumables' six (all eleven 8 ΔE apart in every vision view, 261's follow-up). The badge paints the resolved values from the group's module (surface-badge.ts), so the boot's tokens.ts carries none and the manual's pages, which load no token sheet, get them inline. A consumable hue keeps 8 ΔE from every other badge hue, the Settings tabs', the teams', the squad's and ink's, and 12 from the accent, in every vision view by CIE76 and CIEDE2000, at 3:1 or more on the plates as a graphic (src/ui/tokens/badgeColours.selftest.mjs)

badge-equip-firepower.$use: Equipment: firepower (rammer, stabiliser, GLD, vents, ready rack, fire control, loader kit)

badge-equip-recon.$use: Equipment: recon (optics, binoculars, camouflage net, exhaust baffles, thermal sight)

badge-equip-mobility.$use: Equipment: mobility (rotation, suspension, turret drive, drivetrain)

badge-equip-protection.$use: Equipment: protection (spall liner, skirts, ring guard, mantlet shield)

badge-equip-survival.$use: Equipment: survival (toolbox, wet rack, fuel safety, automatic extinguishers, fire blankets)

badge-cons-repair.$use: Consumables: repair (the field and large repair kits, spare track links): steel

badge-cons-crew.$use: Consumables: crew (first aid kit, field rations): medic rose

badge-cons-fire.$use: Consumables: fire (extinguisher, automatic fire suppression): brick red

badge-cons-ammunition.$use: Consumables: ammunition (ready-rack restock, smoke grenade reload): brass

badge-cons-protection.$use: Consumables: protection (fresh foliage, APS interceptor, IR jammer): violet

surface-badge-paper.$description: Tokens only a light surface reads (the Field Manual printed: chapters.css's print rules): each badge category's frame on paper, its hue darkened to hold 3:1 on paper and white, the eleven 8 ΔE apart in every vision view (badgeColours.selftest), and the glyph's ink on paper. No module: the badge draws the dark-surface hues, and the print rules move the frame and the ink by category

badge-paper-ink.$use: The badge glyph's ink on paper: the dark ink the kit sets on light fills

surface-studio.$description: Tokens only the Studio reads: its direction page's values (bui01/src/pages/09-studio.html)

studio-z.$use: The Studio over the game's canvas and HUD, under modals and toasts

studio-pop-z.$use: The Studio's pickers and its film veil, over its own panels

studio-row-on.$use: A selected outliner, shot or effect row's whole ring, never one coloured edge (09-studio .out .it.on)

studio-knob-ring.$use: A slider's knob seated on its track (09-studio .sl .tr b)

studio-frame-mask.$use: The frame's edge and the dark outside it (09-studio .frame)

studio-clip-fx.$use: An effect's clip on the timeline (09-studio .tl .clip)

surface-battle.$description: Tokens only the battle HUD, load and end screens reads: its direction page's values (bui01/src/pages/06, 06b, 10, 11)

battle-plate-shadow.$use: Every battle HUD plate (the direction's .p: a hairline and a soft drop)

battle-edge-own.$use: The player's own plates (the kill ribbon, the report's best): an accent ring all round, never a stripe (owner 2026-10-25: "stop using the box with one border colored")

battle-nv.$use: The night-vision phosphor: the drone's and the gunship's night view and the scope's (one green, not a state)

battle-pen.$use: The penetration green: the sight's ring and zoom readout where a shot goes through (hud.ts PEN_GREEN) and the shot card's penetrated value (one green with the ring)

battle-text-halo.value: 0 1px 2px oklch(from {surface-scene} l c h / .9),0 0 3px oklch(from {surface-scene} l c h / .65)
battle-text-halo.$use: HUD text over the battlefield itself (the target plate's hull points)

battle-mark-ring.$use: A world mark's keyline (the target plate's diamond, the direction's 06-battle-hud .tgt .dia)

battle-control-on.$use: An active system's underline (the systems row, mouse and touch)

battle-control-label-halo.$use: A system's label over the battlefield

battle-track-callsign.$use: A Latin callsign's tracking in the kill feed, in every locale (its run is marked und-Latn, so zh-CN's letter-spacing 0 leaves it)

battle-chip-warn.$use: A damaged module's or wounded crew member's status chip

battle-fs-11.$use: HUD caps labels (the battle's own sizes: the HUD keeps its 1080p floors at every window, where the shell's --fs steps follow the UI scale)

battle-fs-12.$use: HUD data lines (objective, ping, cause chips)

battle-fs-fig-11.$use: HUD figures and Latin codes (shell types, keycaps, counts): 11 px in every locale, where Chinese lifts the labels to 13

battle-fs-fig-12.$use: HUD figures at 12 px (the hull readout's maximum) in every locale

fs-floor-12.$use: The same floor for a 12 px label: max(var(--fs-floor-12),var(--fs-12))

battle-fs-13.$use: HUD copy (the feed's callsigns, the map's name, the vehicle beside a callsign)

surface-states.$description: Tokens only the boot, loading states and exception pages reads: its direction page's values (bui01/src/pages/the kit)

locale.$description: Per-script typography (SPEC 4.7 CJK, BUI-F8). CSS: :root:lang(<locale>) redefines these tokens, so every component that reads them follows the document language. zh-CN: letter-spacing 0 (caps tracking is a Latin device), the reading leading and measure of CJK text, labels one step up to a 13 px floor, and no outline type (hollow display type stays solid). Latin and digits keep the brand faces through the font stacks.

preset.$description: SPEC 4.6. CSS: :root[data-<axis>=<preset>]; tokens.ts: TOKEN_PRESETS / tokenValue(). No surface hard-codes a team colour.

cvd.$tradeoff: Shape-coded pairs (team colours against each other, the objective neutral and the accent) keep a ΔE floor of 12 in every preset and the views it serves; two SPEC 4.6 presets fall below it and are pinned here, so any change to these colours reopens the decision. (1) Deuteranopia / protanopia: SPEC 4.6's orange enemy (#E69F00) shares the tungsten accent's hue, so enemy~accent falls to 10.0 normal, 7.3 deutan, 3.6 protan, in return for enemy~squad 33.2 -> 57.9 deutan and 28.4 -> 46.4 protan. Not the only option: keeping enemy vermilion and moving squad to paper-50 with the ring (the tritan treatment) keeps enemy~accent at 21.1 deutan / 41.5 protan and gives enemy~squad 52.8 / 50.1, but moves the weak pair to squad~neutral (4.1 / 4.2). tokens.selftest.mjs measures that alternative ($alternative) beside the shipped preset. The shipped preset is SPEC 4.6's, and the accessibility core (BUI-F9) gives players the setting as SPEC 4.6 writes it (the SPEC is law); switching to the alternative is a SPEC amendment, one edit here that the receipt already measures. (2) Tritanopia: squad on paper-50 sits beside the objective neutral (paper-100) at 4.2 normal, 4.0 tritan. In both cases the shape carries the difference (enemy diamond against accent chrome, which is never diamond-shaped; squad dot with its 2 px ring against objective outlines), and the HUD restyle (BUI-H1) owns that shape coding.

high.$description: SPEC 4.6: HUD plates .96, all text ink-1 or ink-2 (7:1), line-3 borders. line-3 itself rises to 3:1 on every surface (SPEC 4.4's non-text floor), and the control border to 4.5:1 so controls stay a step above plate edges

motion.$system: No data-motion attribute is the player's 'System' choice: the $media copy applies only to :root:not([data-motion]). data-motion=reduce collapses the durations whatever the OS says and data-motion=full keeps them whatever it says; the player's choice writes the attribute (the index.html head seed, src/ui/accessibilitySettings.ts) and src/ui/accessibilityMotion.ts turns every prefers-reduced-motion rule in the document on or off to match (SPEC 9: Reduce motion overrides the OS both ways).

runtime.$description: Tokens a player's preference writes at runtime instead of a fixed preset (SPEC 4.6 Custom). the player's choice writes them on :root (inline custom properties under data-<axis>=<preset>: the index.html head seed, src/ui/accessibilitySettings.ts) and src/ui/accessibilityPreferences.ts hands them to setActiveTokens() (tokenSelection.ts), and only after src/ui/colorVision.ts accepts the pair against the SPEC 4.4 contrast and 4.5 colour-vision floors. Every token derived from one is a pure alias of it ({name}), so the cascade and tokens.ts move it alike (gen-tokens fails otherwise); a preset's direct override still beats the derived value, as in the cascade (high contrast sets text-own to ink-1).

alias.$description: Legacy names kept working during migration. Each lives in the file that already owns it as var(--<token>,<fallback>); the fallback equals the token's resolved value (pinned by tokens.selftest.mjs) so pages and fixtures without tokens.css render the same. $was is the value the name shipped with: each name aliases the nearest token of its target's family (colours by the CIE76 distance of the shipped colour over black and over white, durations by milliseconds, easings by the largest difference in progress), and the selftest proves that and prints every shift. SPEC 4.12 names the duration moves (instant 90 -> 80, base 190 -> 220, scene 420 -> 360); slow, drawer and soft follow the nearest-token rule. A $spec entry is a SPEC-named fold that overrides the nearest-token rule: SPEC 4.2 folds #ffd27a (x34) into tungsten-500, so --cot-gold, which colours text, reads the accent text role. The duration and easing moves change motion timing, which still frames cannot show: they are SPEC 4.12's intended changes, not part of the 'no visual change' parity.
